Defeat by ctbparser

Sep 10, 2026

Where does it begin

Recently I read an interesting book on NLP, Semantics by A. Kornai. A draft version of this book can by found on his site. This book, at a moment mentioned a list of resources by language, which led me to ctbparser, that is available on Google Code Archive. It is lastly updated in 2010 and designed with GB2312 encoding, so I figured if I can modernized this program with C++11 standard, and utf-8 encoding. As the title of this article suggested, I failed. Still, this article contains discoveries I found. Hopefully it will be useful for anyone else who share the interest.

Current status of the repository

General information

There is a clone of this repository on GitHub. A very simple README.MD is provided. A slightly more detailed description can be found in readme.html and readme_cn.html. No manual is available.

Compilation

The code of the repository uses a simple “makefile” to compile the program ctbparser. It does not compile directly with today’s default configuration (at least in my case).

A few tweaks should be applied to make it compile correctly:

  • add #include <cstring> to freelist.h (fix memcpy function call);
  • update syntax at crf.cpp:1584, instead of make_pair, use curly brackets syntax: 
    // from
old2new.insert(make_pair<int, int>(it->second, new_mapping_size));
// to
old2new.insert({it->second, new_mapping_size});
  • add #include <unistd.h> to crf.cpp, ctbparser.cpp, crfparser.cpp (fix access unlink function calls)1
  • (optional) add -std=c++11 to CFLAGS in makefile;
  • (optional) remove the linked library -lnsl from the makefile, as it is not needed and not a library installed by default.

If it is compiled successfully, it should work correctly under GB2312 encoding. However, it does not work correctly with utf-8 encoding. As I will mention in a moment, the program is built with this specific encoding in mind. It is hard, if not impossible, to adapt the program for other encoding in a simple way.

Dependencies

The readme.html (and its Chinese version) mentioned:

Word segmentation and POS tagging models are trained using Pocket CRF 0.47, and the dependency parsing model are trained using crfparser 0.10.

The way these dependencies work is, however, different to today’s practice. Instead of using package manager and referencing them verbally, source files are directly copied and modified. Pocket CRF is developed by the same developer of this repository, providing the files like crf.h and crfparser.h. And Pocket CRF is based on crfparser, which has its own version of crf.h, crfparser.h, and other relavant files.

The hard-coded GB2312 encoding

Various implementations of the program ctbparser depend on the GB2312 encoding. Some of these can be adapted to utf-8, and some are not.

Case study: the Trie class

The TrieNode defines a node from the Trie (prefix tree), which is used to store user-defined dictionary. link is a list of pointer that is initialized during node creation, with a fix size of pointer.

// declaration of structure

typedef struct TrieNode{
	int k; //no null link number
	TrieNode **link; //if no branch, link=NULL else *link[95]
	PWORDTYPE wordptr;
}TRIENODE, * PTRIENODE;

// initialization

p->link=(PTRIENODE *)malloc(95*sizeof(PTRIENODE));

The special size of 95 is based on the fact that (cite from Wikipedia):

Characters in GB/T 2312 are arranged in a 94×94 grid […]

With this configuration, each Chinese character can be represented by two nodes of TrieNode. Whereas utf-8 encodes character from 1 to 4 bytes, and cannot be represented to 95 branched per byte.

Despite that, it is possible to create a different Trie structure to serve as a prefix tree for utf-8 encoding. For instance, I modified the structure by implementing a hashtable, and it worked:

struct trie_node_s {
    trie_table_t *table;
    word_type_t *wordptr;
};

struct trie_table_s {
    int table_count[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
    int table_size[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
    unsigned int *keys[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
    trie_node_t **values[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
};

Case study: crfparser

I stuck with the module crfparser, which is used to separate and tag words with a pre-trained model. While it is possible to modify crfparser, the real problem is the “model” it used for the creation of tags. As the model is a binary file, changing its encoding does not make any sense; however, it is encoding specific and only reacts correctly with the GB2312 encoding characters.

Opening the file pos_model_l1 (used by the crfparser) with Codium, regardless its binary nature, the line 12 to 17 looks like this (as by default they are still interpreted as utf-8):

␀␀␀␀␀0:����:
␀␀␀␀␀0:��ȫ\
␀␀␀␀␀0:��~
␀␀␀␀␀0:�����
␀␀␀␀␀0:���
␀␀␀␀␀0:���

By “reopen with GB2312 encoding”:

␀␀␀␀␀0:安排:
␀␀␀␀␀0:安全\
␀␀␀␀␀0:按~
␀␀␀␀␀0:按照�
␀␀␀␀␀0:岸�
␀␀␀␀␀0:案�

It seems like the model file, despite being binary, still influenced by the GB2312 encoding. Giving that the training data of this model is not available with the repository, it is impossible to rebuild the model, which is essential for this program functionality.

Conclusion

It is hard to make the program working with utf-8 encoding, as recreating the model used by crfparser is a difficult, as one need to understand the crfparser repo, and create a new model with utf-8 encoding. On the other hand, if one has to make the program work with utf-8 encoding, my suggestion is to wrap the entier program within a translation program.

For example, imaging the following pseudo code:

void decode_string_utf8(const char *utf8_in, char *utf8_out) {
	char gb2312in[10000], gb2312out[10000];
	utf8_gb2312(utf8_in, gb2312in);
	decode_string(gb2312in, gb2312out);
	gb2312_utf8(gb2312out, utf8_out);
}

As that is not my interest, I am here to accept my defeat.

Appendix

Modified Trie class

As part of my implementation, I wrote a new version of Trie class for utf-8 characters. Here is my implementation:

// trie.h

#ifndef TRIE_H
#define TRIE_H

const int WORD_MAXLENGTH             = 1000;
const int POS_MAXLENGTH              = 12;
const int POS_FREQ_MAXLENGTH         = 5;
const int TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE        = 128;
const int TRIE_HASHTABLE_INIT_LENGTH = 1;

typedef struct pos_freq_s {
    char pos[POS_MAXLENGTH];
    double freq;
} pos_freq_t;

typedef struct word_type_s {
    char *word;
    double freq; // sum of posfreq;
    pos_freq_t posfreq[POS_FREQ_MAXLENGTH];
} word_type_t;

typedef struct trie_node_s trie_node_t;
typedef struct trie_table_s trie_table_t;

struct trie_node_s {
    trie_table_t *table;
    word_type_t *wordptr;
};

struct trie_table_s {
    int table_count[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
    int table_size[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
    unsigned int *keys[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
    trie_node_t **values[TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE];
};

word_type_t *word_type_init(const char *word);
void word_type_destroy(word_type_t *word);
void word_type_update(word_type_t *word, const char *pos, double freq);

trie_node_t *trie_node_init();
void trie_node_destroy(trie_node_t *node);
trie_node_t *trie_node_add(trie_node_t *node, const char *utf8_string,
                           const char *utf8_rest, const char *pos, double freq);
trie_node_t *trie_node_get(trie_node_t *node, const char *utf8_string);

trie_table_t *trie_table_init();
void trie_table_destroy(trie_table_t *table);
trie_node_t *trie_table_add(trie_table_t *table, unsigned int key);
trie_node_t *trie_table_get(trie_table_t *table, unsigned int key);

class Trie {
    private:
    trie_node_t *root;

    public:
    Trie();
    ~Trie();
    bool load(const char *filename);
    void insert(const char *word, const char *pos, double freq);
    // void search(const char *word);
    word_type_t *search(const char *word, trie_node_t *node = nullptr);

    void get_best_pos(word_type_t *word, char *pos);
    double get_freq(word_type_t *word, const char *pos = nullptr);
    double get_freq(const char *word, const char *pos = nullptr);
};
#endif


// trie.cpp

#include "trie.h"
#include "fun.h"
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

// Source - https://stackoverflow.com/a/12996028
// Posted by Thomas Mueller, modified by community. See post 'Timeline' for
// change history Retrieved 2026-09-08, License - CC BY-SA 4.0

unsigned hash_uint(unsigned x) {
    x = ((x >> 16) ^ x) * 0x45d9f3bu;
    x = ((x >> 16) ^ x) * 0x45d9f3bu;
    x = (x >> 16) ^ x;
    return x;
}

static unsigned int utf8_to_uint(const char *utf8_char) {
    char utf8_buffer[5] = { 0 };
    if (utf8_char_cpy(utf8_char, utf8_buffer) < 0) {
        return 0;
    }
    unsigned int value = (utf8_buffer[0] << 24) + (utf8_buffer[1] << 16) +
                         (utf8_buffer[2] << 8) + (utf8_buffer[3] << 0);

    return value;
}

word_type_t *word_type_init(const char *word) {
    if (word == nullptr) return nullptr;

    word_type_t *word_type = (word_type_t *)calloc(1, sizeof(word_type_t));
    word_type->word        = strdup(word);

    return word_type;
}

void word_type_update(word_type_t *word, const char *pos, double freq) {
    if (word == nullptr || pos == nullptr) return;

    for (int i = 0; i < POS_FREQ_MAXLENGTH; i++) {
        if (strncmp(word->posfreq[i].pos, pos, POS_MAXLENGTH) == 0) {
            // already has the pos data, should be a mistake
            printf("fail to update word freq with word %s and pos %s: another "
                   "entry existed",
                   word->word, pos);
            return;
        }
        if (strlen(word->posfreq[i].pos) == 0) {
            strncpy(word->posfreq[i].pos, pos, POS_MAXLENGTH);
            word->posfreq[i].freq = freq;
            word->freq += freq;
            return;
        }
    }
    puts("Warning: max length of POS_FREQ_MAXLENGTH exceeded");
}

void word_type_destroy(word_type_t *word) {
    if (word == nullptr) return;
    if (word->word != nullptr) {
        free(word->word);
    }
}

trie_node_t *trie_node_init() {
    trie_node_t *node = (trie_node_t *)calloc(1, sizeof(trie_node_t));
    return node;
}

void trie_node_destroy(trie_node_t *node) {
    if (node == nullptr) return;
    if (node->table != nullptr) {
        trie_table_destroy(node->table);
    }
    if (node->wordptr) {
        word_type_destroy(node->wordptr);
    }
}

trie_node_t *trie_node_add(trie_node_t *node, const char *utf8_string,
                           const char *utf8_rest, const char *pos,
                           double freq) {

    if (node == nullptr || utf8_string == nullptr || utf8_rest == nullptr ||
        pos == nullptr) {
        return nullptr;
    }

    char utf8_char[5];
    const char *rest = utf8_char_pop(utf8_rest, utf8_char);

    if (node->table == nullptr) {
        node->table = trie_table_init();
    }

    // find child with given utf8 character
    trie_node_t *child = trie_table_add(node->table, utf8_to_uint(utf8_char));

    if (rest != nullptr && rest[0] != '\0') {
        trie_node_add(child, utf8_string, rest, pos, freq);
    } else {
        child->wordptr = word_type_init(utf8_string);
        word_type_update(child->wordptr, pos, freq);
    }

    return child;
}

trie_node_t *trie_node_get(trie_node_t *node, const char *utf8_string) {
    if (node == nullptr || utf8_string == nullptr) return nullptr;

    char utf8_char[5];
    const char *rest = utf8_char_pop(utf8_string, utf8_char);

    // find child with given utf8 character
    trie_node_t *child = trie_table_get(node->table, utf8_to_uint(utf8_char));

    if (child == nullptr) return nullptr;

    if (rest == nullptr || rest[0] == '\0') {
        return child;
    } else {
        return trie_node_get(child, rest);
    }
}

trie_table_t *trie_table_init() {
    trie_table_t *table = (trie_table_t *)calloc(1, sizeof(trie_table_t));
    return table;
}

void trie_table_destroy(trie_table_t *table) {
    if (table == nullptr) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE; i++) {
        if (table->table_size[i] <= 0) continue;
        if (table->keys[i] == nullptr || table->values[i] == nullptr) {
            printf("Warning: unexpected nullptr in hashtable in file %s\n at "
                   "line %d",
                   __FILE__, __LINE__);
            continue;
        }

        for (int j = 0; j < table->table_count[i]; j++) {
            trie_node_t *node = table->values[i][j];
            trie_node_destroy(node);
        }

        free(table->keys[i]);
        free(table->values[i]);
    }
    free(table);
}

trie_node_t *trie_table_add(trie_table_t *table, unsigned int key) {
    if (table == nullptr) return nullptr;

    int table_index = hash_uint(key) % TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE;

    for (int i = 0; i < table->table_count[table_index]; i++) {
        if (table->keys[table_index][i] == key) {
            // find a node with given key, return the node
            return table->values[table_index][i];
        }
    }

    // no present key with given value, add a new one

    // make sure the table is large enough
    if (table->table_size[table_index] <= 0) {
        // create table if no table existed

        table->keys[table_index] =
            (unsigned int *)calloc(TRIE_HASHTABLE_INIT_LENGTH, sizeof(int));
        table->values[table_index] = (trie_node_t **)calloc(
            TRIE_HASHTABLE_INIT_LENGTH, sizeof(trie_node_t *));
        table->table_size[table_index] = 1;

    } else if (table->table_size[table_index] ==
               table->table_count[table_index]) {
        // table full, resize table

        table->keys[table_index] = (unsigned int *)realloc(
            table->keys[table_index],
            2 * table->table_count[table_index] * sizeof(int));
        table->values[table_index] = (trie_node_t **)realloc(
            table->values[table_index],
            2 * table->table_count[table_index] * sizeof(trie_node_t *));
        table->table_size[table_index] *= 2;
    }

    // add new node
    trie_node_t *node = trie_node_init();
    int elem_index    = table->table_count[table_index];
    table->table_count[table_index]++;
    table->keys[table_index][elem_index]   = key;
    table->values[table_index][elem_index] = node;

    return node;
}

trie_node_t *trie_table_get(trie_table_t *table, unsigned int key) {
    if (table == nullptr) return nullptr;

    int table_index = hash_uint(key) % TRIE_HASHTABLE_SIZE;

    if (table->keys[table_index] == nullptr ||
        table->values[table_index] == nullptr) {
        return nullptr;
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < table->table_count[table_index]; i++) {
        if (table->keys[table_index][i] == key) {
            // find a node with given key, return the node
            return table->values[table_index][i];
        }
    }

    return nullptr;
}

Trie::Trie() {
    root = trie_node_init();
}

Trie::~Trie() {
    trie_node_destroy(root);
}

bool Trie::load(const char *filename) {
    FILE *file = fopen(filename, "r");
    if (file == nullptr) {
        perror("fopen");
        return false;
    }

    char line_buffer[256];
    char word_buffer[128];
    char pos_buffer[24];
    double freq = 0;

    int read_bytes = 0;
    while (fgets(line_buffer, sizeof(line_buffer), file)) {
        read_bytes =
            sscanf(line_buffer, "%s\t%s\t%lf", word_buffer, pos_buffer, &freq);
        if (read_bytes) {
            insert(word_buffer, pos_buffer, freq);
        }
    }

    fclose(file);
    return true;
}

void Trie::insert(const char *word, const char *pos, double freq) {
    trie_node_add(root, word, word, pos, freq);
}

// void search(const char *word) {
//     // TODO
// }

word_type_t *Trie::search(const char *word, trie_node_t *node) {
    if (word == nullptr) return nullptr;

    if (node == nullptr) {
        node = root;
    }

    trie_node_t *node2 = trie_node_get(node, word);
    if (node2 == nullptr) return nullptr;
    return node2->wordptr;
}

void Trie::get_best_pos(word_type_t *word, char *pos) {
    if (word == nullptr || pos == nullptr) return;
    if (strlen(pos) != 0) {
        puts("Warning: pos buffer is not empty");
        return;
    }
    if (strlen(word->posfreq[0].pos) == 0) {
        puts("Warning: no valid pos info for given word");
        return;
    }
    double freq = word->posfreq[0].freq;
    strcpy(pos, word->posfreq[0].pos);

    for (int i = 0; i < POS_FREQ_MAXLENGTH; i++) {
        if (word->posfreq[i].freq <= freq) continue;

        strcpy(pos, word->posfreq[i].pos);
    }
}

double Trie::get_freq(word_type_t *word, const char *pos) {
    if (word == nullptr) return -1;

    if (pos == nullptr) {
        return word->freq;
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < POS_FREQ_MAXLENGTH; i++) {
        if (strncpy(word->posfreq[i].pos, pos, POS_MAXLENGTH) == 0) {
            // found
            return word->posfreq[i].freq;
        }
    }

    return -1;
}

double Trie::get_freq(const char *word, const char *pos) {
    if (word == nullptr) return -1;

    word_type_t *word_type = search(word);
    return get_freq(word_type, pos);
}


// functions defined in `fun.h`

int utf8_char_len(const char *p);
int utf8_char_cpy(const char *src, char *buffer);
bool utf8_char_comp(const char *c1, const char *c2);
bool utf8_char_contain(const char *s, const char *c);
const char *utf8_char_pop(const char *s, char *c);

int utf8_char_len(const char *p) {
    // supposing `p` point to an utf8 array, move to the next utf8 char
    if (p == nullptr || p[0] == '\0') return 0;

    int skip  = -1;
    char head = p[0];

    if ((head & 0b10000000) == 0b00000000) {
        // first bit 0, valid utf8 char with length 1
        skip = 1;
    } else if ((head & 0b11100000) == 0b11000000) {
        // first three bits 110, valid utf8 char with length 2
        skip = 2;
    } else if ((head & 0b11110000) == 0b11100000) {
        // first four bits 1110, valid utf8 char with length 3
        skip = 3;
    } else if ((head & 0b11111000) == 0b11110000) {
        // first five bits 11110, valid utf8 char with length 4
        skip = 4;
    } else {
        // not a valid uft8 char
        return -1;
    }

    return skip;
}

int utf8_char_cpy(const char *src, char *buffer) {
    int char_len = utf8_char_len(src);
    if (char_len < 0) {
        return -1;
    }

    strncpy(buffer, src, char_len);
    return char_len;
}

bool utf8_char_comp(const char *c1, const char *c2) {
    int c1_len = utf8_char_len(c1);
    int c2_len = utf8_char_len(c1);

    if (c1_len < 0 || c1_len != c2_len) {
        // either c1 or c2 is not valid utf8 char,
        // or their length (byte) is different
        return false;
    }

    // compare n byte
    bool is_same = (strncmp(c1, c2, c1_len) == 0);
    return is_same;
}

bool utf8_char_contain(const char *s, const char *c) {
    int len = strlen(s);
    int i   = 0;
    while (i < len) {
        if (utf8_char_comp(s, c)) return true;
        i += utf8_char_len(s + i);
    }
    return false;
}

const char *utf8_char_pop(const char *s, char *c) {
    int i = utf8_char_cpy(s, c);
    return s + i;
}

  1. unistd.h is POSIX operating system API, so equivalent approach should be applied on Windows. ↩
